title: Google Stock News (Oct 19, 2026): GOOGL Falls 2.5% to $340.59
summary: Alphabet (GOOGL) closed at $340.59 on Oct 16, down 2.47%, as the Nasdaq fell 2.15%. What moved the stock ahead of Oct 28 earnings.
body_markdown:
## Why Google Stock Fell


None of the sources we fetched names a company-specific trigger for Friday's decline, so the move reads best against the wider market, where chip and software names such as AMD, Micron and Oracle fell 4% to 6%. Weekend coverage focused on Alphabet's business rather than the drop. According to[The Motley Fool](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/prediction-alphabet-report-google-cloud-120500989.html) , shares have fallen since reaching an all-time high in the spring, and Alphabet reported negative free cash flow last quarter for the first time as a public company.


Separately, Simply Wall St. reported that American Electric Power is committing about $4 billion to a 702-megawatt fuel cell project near Cheyenne, Wyoming, backed by a 20-year power purchase agreement with Google, per[Simply Wall St.](https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/articles/american-electric-power-company-aep-231338036.html) .


## GOOGL Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Google Cloud sales rose 82% to $24.8 billion in the second quarter of 2026, as reported by[The Motley Fool](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/1-analyst-thinks-alphabet-stock-163500200.html) .
- Per The Motley Fool, Alphabet cited a $514 billion revenue backlog and expects to recognize half of it over the next 24 months.
- Alphabet has begun selling its Tensor Processing Units to other AI companies, and CEO Sundar Pichai said it will deliver TPUs to a select group of customers in their own data centers.
- The 20-year Google power deal with AEP adds dedicated capacity for its data center buildout.


### Risks


- Alphabet plans to spend about $200 billion on AI infrastructure this year, and investor concern about industry AI spending could weigh on sentiment.
- CFO Anat Ashkenazi said Alphabet would expand third-party capacity in the third quarter as a bridging strategy, which she warned will pressure Google Cloud's margin.
- Free cash flow turned negative last quarter, and The Motley Fool expects it to fall further into the red.


The next confirmed event is third-quarter results on October 28, when the[earnings report](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/how-to-read-an-earnings-report/) will update the Google Cloud growth and capital spending figures above.
